terms.name: 12 column grid
terms.definition: The web's default column count, chosen because twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.

terms.name: Action sheet
terms.definition: A modal list of choices that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen in response to something you just did, with cancel at the end.

terms.name: Anticipation
terms.definition: A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.

terms.name: Attribute editor
terms.definition: A repeating row of key and value fields with add and remove controls, used for tags, headers and other open ended pairs.

terms.name: Bidirectional text
terms.definition: Text mixing a right-to-left script with left-to-right runs such as numbers or Latin words, where each run keeps its own direction.

terms.name: Bulk actions
terms.definition: Selecting several rows and applying one command to all of them, usually through a bar that appears once a selection exists and reports its count.

terms.name: Cassette futurism
terms.definition: The analog future of late 1970s science fiction: beige and putty plastic, chunky toggles and rocker switches, amber or green CRT readouts, and monochrome bitmap type.

terms.name: Chroma
terms.definition: Colourfulness measured in absolute terms rather than as a percentage of the maximum, so a light pastel and a dark ink can be compared on one scale.

terms.name: Color harmony
terms.definition: A rule for choosing colours by their positions on the wheel, such as complementary or analogous or triadic, so a palette holds together by construction.

terms.name: Command palette
terms.definition: A keyboard-summoned overlay whose single search box finds and runs any command or destination in an application by name.

terms.name: Container
terms.definition: A wrapper that caps how wide content can get and adds the side padding that keeps it off the viewport edges.

terms.name: Cover
terms.definition: A layout primitive that fills at least the viewport height, centring a principal element vertically with optional header and footer pinned above and below.

terms.name: De Stijl
terms.definition: A style built only from black rules, rectangular fields, and the three primaries on white, arranged asymmetrically with no curves and no diagonals.

terms.name: Dimensionality
terms.definition: Giving interface objects a believable place in depth by folding, layering or flipping them, so a reader can tell where something went and where it will come back from.

terms.name: Drag and drop
terms.definition: Picking up an object, moving it under continuous pointer or finger contact, and releasing it over a target that accepts it.

terms.name: Dynamic Type
terms.definition: A platform feature that scales interface text to a size the reader chose in system settings, with layouts expected to reflow around it.

terms.name: Endowed progress
terms.definition: Starting a progress meter part filled, so the reader feels they are continuing something already begun rather than starting from nothing.

terms.name: Fade through
terms.definition: Material's transition for unrelated views: the outgoing view fades out completely before the incoming one fades in while scaling up slightly.

terms.name: Fine print
terms.definition: Qualifying text set small and set last, carrying the conditions that the larger claim above it leaves out.

terms.name: Fluid space scale
terms.definition: A spacing ramp whose every step interpolates between a minimum and a maximum viewport, so gaps grow smoothly with the screen instead of jumping at breakpoints.

terms.name: Font pairing
terms.definition: Choosing two or more typefaces that work together, usually one expressive and one neutral, with enough contrast to read as a deliberate choice.

terms.name: Gantt chart
terms.definition: One row per task with a bar along a time axis, the bar showing when the work runs and lines between bars showing what waits for what.

terms.name: Graph layout
terms.definition: Placing the nodes of a wired diagram by algorithm rather than by hand: layered for a flow, radial for a hub, force-directed for a mesh that has no direction.

terms.name: Height animation
terms.definition: Animating a container between collapsed and its content's natural size, long impossible because height auto did not interpolate and now opened up by interpolate-size and calc-size().

terms.name: Hoverable, dismissible, persistent
terms.definition: The three conditions content revealed on hover or focus must meet: reachable with the pointer, dismissible without moving focus, and not self-closing.

terms.name: Increased contrast
terms.definition: A user preference for more contrast than a theme's default, honoured by strengthening borders, text, and state colours rather than by shifting hues.

terms.name: Interstitial
terms.definition: A full screen placed between two steps of a flow, carrying a message, an advert, or a warning that the reader must pass through to continue.

terms.name: Key sequence
terms.definition: A shortcut typed as an ordered run of presses, where the first key opens a mode and the next chooses within it.

terms.name: Layout margins
terms.definition: The reserved space between a container's edge and its content, sized by the system so content never touches the edge of the screen.

terms.name: linear() easing
terms.definition: An easing written as a list of sampled stops rather than a curve, which lets CSS express springs and bounces that no cubic bezier can describe.

terms.name: Lorem ipsum
terms.definition: Scrambled pseudo-Latin placeholder text used so a layout can be judged on its shape and texture before the real copy exists.

terms.name: Mega menu
terms.definition: A large navigation panel that drops from a top level item and shows many links at once, grouped into columns with headings.

terms.name: Minimap
terms.definition: A shrunken overview of a long document or canvas beside the scrollbar, with a box showing which part is currently on screen.

terms.name: Motion choreography
terms.definition: The plan for how several animating elements relate in time and space, deciding what leads, what follows, and what stays still.

terms.name: Neon glow
terms.definition: A saturated colour surrounded by layered soft shadows of the same hue, so type or a border reads as a lit tube against a dark surface.

terms.name: OKLCH
terms.definition: A colour notation of lightness, chroma and hue built on Oklab, where changing the hue leaves the perceived lightness alone and equal steps look equal.

terms.name: Origin-aware animation
terms.definition: Scaling or fading a panel out of the control that opened it by putting its transform origin on that anchor, so the panel reads as belonging to its trigger.

terms.name: Pan
terms.definition: Moving the viewport across content in any direction while keeping contact, so the content feels anchored to the finger or cursor.

terms.name: Pinch to zoom
terms.definition: Two fingers moving apart or together on a surface to scale content up or down, with the scale tracking the distance between them.

terms.name: Predictive back
terms.definition: A back gesture that reveals the destination underneath while the finger is still down, so the swipe can be finished or abandoned once the reader has seen where it goes.

terms.name: Progressive profiling
terms.definition: Collecting profile details a few at a time across separate visits, instead of demanding the whole record in one long form at registration.

terms.name: Radio group
terms.definition: A set of mutually exclusive options, each with its own label and control, exactly one of which can be chosen.

terms.name: Reduced transparency
terms.definition: A user preference asking for opaque surfaces instead of blur and translucency, honoured by swapping frosted layers for solid fills.

terms.name: Rich text toolbar
terms.definition: The strip of formatting controls above or beside an editor, whose buttons report their state from wherever the caret sits.

terms.name: Scaffold
terms.definition: The frame that positions an app's persistent regions, its bars, panes and body, so each screen drops content into named slots instead of inventing its own arrangement.

terms.name: Scroll-triggered animation
terms.definition: An animation that scroll position only starts, after which it runs on its own clock and does not rewind when the reader scrolls back up.

terms.name: Semantic zoom
terms.definition: Switching between two views of the same content, a zoomed out view of group headings and a zoomed in view of individual items, instead of scaling pixels.

terms.name: Signifier
terms.definition: The visible cue that advertises an affordance, such as a grip texture, an underline, or a shadow that says this can be pressed.

terms.name: Sneak into basket
terms.definition: Adding an item the buyer never chose, an insurance, a donation, a warranty, into the cart through a preselected control found earlier in the flow.

terms.name: Split button
terms.definition: A two part control where the main area runs a default action and an attached arrow opens a menu of related alternatives.

terms.name: Status bar
terms.definition: A thin strip along the edge of a window or screen that reports state and offers only minor actions, never the primary ones.

terms.name: Stylistic set
terms.definition: A numbered bundle of alternate glyphs inside a font, switched on as a group to change the look of certain letters.

terms.name: Switcher
terms.definition: A layout primitive that flips between a row and a column at a threshold it works out from its own width, with no media query involved.

terms.name: Terrazzo
terms.definition: A background pattern of small irregular chips scattered on a plain field, copied from poured stone flooring and used flat and multicolored behind interface content.

terms.name: Tiny tweaks
terms.definition: The lightest responsive pattern: a single column design that only adjusts type size, image size and margins as the screen changes.

terms.name: Transcript
terms.definition: A full text version of time based media, readable without playing it and searchable by both people and machines.

terms.name: Typographic color
terms.definition: The overall lightness or darkness a block of text produces when you stop reading it and look at it as a grey texture.

terms.name: VHS aesthetic
terms.definition: A look that imitates a worn videotape: tracking bands, smeared color bleeding past edges, interlace comb artifacts, and burned-in timecode or REC overlays.

terms.name: Widget
terms.definition: A small, glanceable view of an app placed on a system surface such as a home screen or desktop, sized in fixed slots rather than freely.

terms.name: Zigzag layout
terms.definition: Alternating rows that flip which side the image and the text sit on, so the eye zigzags down a list of features.
